answer: Cumulative Resource Aging Proof Agents must continuously weave a cryptographic thread through daily computational puzzles to maintain active status. Each solved block yields a digital pearl bound to that specific execution history. An attacker cloning an agent to bypass load limits cannot split this accumulated history. To forge a duplicate identity, the attacker must independently duplicate months of continuous processor work and electricity expenditure for every single clone, making mass Sybil creation economically unfeasible.
